summary: This continuation proves the prime-order generalized Segal conjecture from the Steenrod algebra, the Singer construction and controlled Adams convergence. nodes.title: Extended powers of spectra
nodes.statement: For k≥1 and a subgroup G≤Σ_k, D_G(E) is the homotopy orbit spectrum (E^{⊗k})_{hG}, with G acting by the symmetry of the smash product, including its suspension signs. Write D_k=D_{Σ_k} and D_{C_p} for the cyclic subgroup generated by a fixed p-cycle. This is a functor on spectra, not a fixed-point construction.
hypotheses: k≥1; G≤Σ_k; all tensor products are derived smash products in Sp.
proofSteps: Use the coherent permutation action from the symmetric monoidal structure, then take homotopy orbits.
Obtain subgroup comparison maps and finite-cover transfers from the imported orbit/norm formalism.
Track the actual permutation representation on suspension coordinates; the underlying suspension by kn alone loses equivariance.
acceptance: D_G preserves equivalences and filtered colimits; its mixed-summand expansion is indexed by G-orbits of words in the summands.

nodes.title: Cyclic Tate coefficients and Weyl weights
nodes.statement: For the trivial C_p-action, the cohomologically graded Tate coefficient algebra of HF_2 is F_2[s^{±1}], |s|=−1. For odd p it is F_p[t^{±1}]⊗Λ(e), |t|=−2 and |e|=−1. Choose e so that t^{−1}e is the positive degree-one group-cohomology generator. Under the normalizer quotient W=F_p^×, a acts on t by a and fixes e; therefore invariants are F_p[t^{±(p−1)}]⊗Λ(e). For HZ the Tate groups are F_p in even degrees and zero in odd degrees, and W-invariants occur in degrees divisible by 2(p−1). These are graded coefficient rings, not rings of arbitrary ungraded infinite series.
hypotheses: p prime; W=N_{Σ_p}(C_p)/C_p; coefficient actions are trivial.
proofSteps: Use the alternating maps g−1 and N in the complete cyclic resolution; cup products give the Laurent generator and, at odd p, the exterior generator.
Compute the normalizer action on H¹(C_p;F_p) by conjugation, then choose t and e as above.
For HZ use the same resolution and reduction; take W-invariants since |W| is invertible on these p-primary groups.
acceptance: At p=3 the invariant even generator has degree −4, not −2.
The odd generator e has degree −1 and weight zero, while t^{−1}e has weight a^{−1}.

sources.locator: §I.1, p.218; §IV.1, discussion before Theorem IV.1.15, p.332

nodes.title: Stable Steenrod operations
nodes.statement: Construct stable natural additive operations Sq^i:H^q(−;F_2)→H^{q+i}(−;F_2), and for odd p operations P^i:H^q(−;F_p)→H^{q+2i(p−1)}(−;F_p) and the coefficient Bockstein β of degree one. Here i≥0, Sq^0=P^0=id, and β is from 0→Z/p→Z/p²→Z/p→0. Equivalently these are maps HF_p→Σ^dHF_p. Use the standard normalization of the cyclic extended-power operation; define negative-index Sq and P to be zero. Instability is a property on cohomology of spaces, not on every class of an arbitrary spectrum.
proofSteps: Apply the E∞ multiplication of HF_p to cyclic extended powers of its suspensions. Orient the permutation representation mod p: at odd p a p-cycle has positive determinant, and mod 2 signs disappear.
Use the cyclic coefficient basis to select the usual normalized components. Prove suspension compatibility so they represent maps of spectra.
Use the external-product comparison to identify the Bockstein and to prove naturality and the instability tests.
acceptance: For any space and homogeneous x of degree q≥0: Sq^i x=0 for i>q and Sq^q x=x²; P^i x=0 for 2i>q and P^{q/2}x=x^p when q is even.
Sq¹ is the mod-2 coefficient Bockstein.

nodes.title: The mod-p Steenrod algebra
nodes.statement: Let A_p be the graded F_p-algebra of all stable mod-p cohomology operations, with multiplication given by composition (the right-hand operation acts first). Give its presentation by Sq^i at p=2 and by P^i,β at odd p. The unit is Sq⁰ or P⁰ and β²=0. For a<2b, Sq^a Sq^b=Σ_j binom(b−j−1,a−2j) Sq^{a+b−j}Sq^j. At odd p, for a<pb, P^aP^b=Σ_j (−1)^{a+j}binom((p−1)(b−j)−1,a−pj)P^{a+b−j}P^j. For a≤pb, P^aβP^b=Σ_j (−1)^{a+j}binom((p−1)(b−j),a−pj)βP^{a+b−j}P^j +Σ_j (−1)^{a+j−1}binom((p−1)(b−j)−1,a−pj−1)P^{a+b−j}βP^j. Indices j are nonnegative and binomial coefficients with negative lower entry vanish. All coefficients are reduced mod p. The coproduct is determined by Cartan: ΔSq^n=Σ_{i+j=n}Sq^i⊗Sq^j, ΔP^n=Σ_{i+j=n}P^i⊗P^j and Δβ=β⊗1+1⊗β, with graded tensor signs.
proofSteps: Prove Cartan using external powers and the diagonal; use iterated powers and subgroup transfers for Adem. Reduce every word to an admissible word by those relations.

Use Eilenberg–MacLane representability and suspension to express stable operations as the stabilized additive universal classes. Compute their indecomposable duals by the iterated bar construction: suspension, divided powers and transpotence give the canonical words (Cartan Exposé 15, Theorems 1–2).

Pair the iterated Steenrod operations with these canonical words. Induct on stable degree and lexicographic order: top-power normalization gives the diagonal entries, instability gives the lower-triangular zeros, and Bockstein distinguishes the second species (Cartan Exposé 16, Theorem 1 bis). This proves independence and exhaustiveness in the stable range without using the subsequent Milnor dual theorem.
Construct the connected graded Hopf structure from external products and composition. The full stable operation algebra is thereby identified with the displayed presentation.
acceptance: The algebra acts on H*(B;F_p) for every spectrum B, without an instability hypothesis.
The graded tensor product of A_p-modules uses the displayed coproduct and Koszul signs.

nodes.title: Milnor dual and finite Hopf subalgebras
nodes.statement: The graded dual A_{p,*}=⊕_d Hom_Fp(A_p^d,F_p) is F_2[ξ_1,ξ_2,…] with |ξ_i|=2^i−1 when p=2, and Λ(τ_0,τ_1,…)⊗F_p[ξ_1,ξ_2,…] with |τ_i|=2p^i−1 and |ξ_i|=2(p^i−1) when p is odd. Fix ξ_0=1 and the coproduct convention Δξ_n=Σ_{i=0}^n ξ_{n−i}^{p^i}⊗ξ_i and Δτ_n=τ_n⊗1+Σ_{i=0}^n ξ_{n−i}^{p^i}⊗τ_i. Each degree is finite-dimensional. The standard finite sub-Hopf algebras exhaust A_p: at p=2 use generators Sq¹,…,Sq^{2^n}; at odd p use β,P¹,…,P^{p^{n−1}} (n=0 means the exterior algebra on β). A_p is free over each of these subalgebras.
hypotheses: All duals are graded degreewise duals, not the ungraded dual of an infinite direct sum.
proofSteps: Construct the dual generators by the coaction on BC_p classes and calculate their coproducts from coassociativity.
Compare the resulting monomial pairing with admissible operations by a triangular argument.

Obtain the finite Hopf pieces from the truncated dual quotients; use the monomial basis to establish freeness. Iterate the Künneth isomorphism for HF_p-homology to deduce that every degree of π*(HF_p^{⊗p}) is finite.
acceptance: For p=2, (HF_2)_*(HF_2)=F_2[ξ_1,ξ_2,…]; in particular degrees 0,1,2 are one-dimensional.
For odd p, the first odd dual generator is τ_0 in degree one; it cannot be omitted when forming the Adams cobar complex.

nodes.title: The mod-p Adams resolution
nodes.statement: For H=HF_p, let I=fib(S→H). For a spectrum B form the tower B_s=I^{⊗s}⊗B, s≥0, with B_0=B, and structure maps induced by I→S. The cofiber at filtration s is H⊗I^{⊗s}⊗B. Equivalently use the augmented H-cobar cosimplicial spectrum B⊗H^{⊗(n+1)}. Its normalized exact couple gives the mod-p Adams spectral sequence. When B is bounded below with degreewise finite-dimensional mod-p homology, its E₂ page is identified as E_2^{s,t}=Ext_{A_p}^{s,t}(H*(B;F_p),F_p), with d_r:(s,t)↦(s+r,t+r−1) and stem t−s.
proofSteps: Use the unit S→H and derived smash to form the functorial tower and its cofiber sequences.

For B bounded below and mod-p degreewise finite type, identify the E₁ complex with the normalized cobar resolution using the H-coaction and degreewise duality; pass to the graded Ext description. The tower itself needs neither hypothesis.
Relate the partial totalizations of the cosimplicial resolution to the exact-couple tower. Convergence is a separate theorem below.
acceptance: No convergence is inferred just from the displayed E₂ page.
The tower is defined for every B, but this cohomological Ext identification is asserted only in the bounded-below degreewise finite-type range.

sources.match: The canonical Adams resolutions exist without finiteness; the cohomological Ext identification here uses the bounded-below finite-type hypotheses of §2.1.

nodes.title: Finite-type Adams convergence
nodes.statement: If B is bounded below and H_i(B;F_p) is finite-dimensional for each i, the mod-p Adams spectral sequence has E₂^{s,t}=Ext_{A_p}^{s,t}(H*(B;F_p),F_p) and converges strongly to π_{t−s}(B_p^∧), with its complete Hausdorff Adams filtration. Maps of such spectra induce maps of these filtered abutments. This theorem does not assert strong convergence for arbitrary unbounded B.
hypotheses: B is bounded below; each mod-p homology group is finite-dimensional.
proofSteps: Identify H-nilpotent completion with derived p-completion in this bounded-below finite-type range by the Adams tower and the mod-p detection criterion.
Use connectivity and the finite-type bounds on successive cobar terms to verify the derived-limit and completeness conditions of the imported convergence criterion.
Identify the associated filtration, then use separated completeness for the comparison of filtered abutments.
acceptance: An E₂ isomorphism between the relevant strongly convergent spectral sequences gives an isomorphism of the p-completed homotopy groups.
For B=HF_p the abutment is F_p in degree zero and zero elsewhere.

nodes.statement: For a specified inverse tower Y_0←Y_1←⋯, define H_c^q(Y_•;F_p)=colim_n H^q(Y_n;F_p), with its graded A_p-action. It comes with the comparison to H^q(holim Y_n;F_p) induced by projections. This construction depends on a tower and is invariant under cofinal reindexing and pro-equivalence; it is not defined to be the ordinary cohomology of the inverse limit.
proofSteps: Take the degreewise filtered colimit in graded A_p-modules.
Construct the comparison by the compatible inverse-limit projections and prove cofinal invariance.
For the Tate application use the specified Singer approximation tower below, not the ordinary homotopy limit as a replacement definition.
acceptance: Every use of H_c names its approximation tower.

nodes.title: Adams spectral sequence for inverse limits
nodes.statement: Let Y_• be a countable inverse tower, each Y_n bounded below and of finite type over F_p; no uniform lower bound in n is required. There is a natural spectral sequence E₂^{s,t}=Ext_{A_p}^{s,t}(H_c^*(Y_•;F_p),F_p) strongly converging to π_{t−s}((holim_nY_n)_p^∧). Its complete Hausdorff filtration and naturality allow the comparison theorem with the Adams spectral sequence of a bounded-below finite-type source mapping compatibly to this tower.
hypotheses: Each individual stage is bounded below and degreewise mod-p finite type.
proofSteps: Take the compatible Adams resolutions of all Y_n, retaining both tower indices. Degreewise finite-type cohomology makes the finite-stage dual groups compact Hausdorff.

Prove exactness of countable inverse limits in this compact setting using finite intersection compactness; this controls the derived limits of the resolution and exact-couple terms. Do not claim arbitrary inverse limits of abelian groups are exact.
Identify the E₂ term by the dual cobar complex of colim H*Y_n; completion commutes with the spectral inverse limit via the imported function-spectrum model.
Verify the complete-convergence criterion, including the vanishing obstruction terms, as in the source proof, then identify the filtered abutment.
acceptance: The constant tower recovers finite-type Adams convergence.
Applied to the Singer tower, the output is π*((T_pB)_p^∧), although T_pB need not be bounded below.

nodes.title: The cohomological Singer construction
nodes.statement: For a graded left A_p-module M, define the exact functor R_+(M) with Σ^{−1}R_+(M)=F_2[x^{±1}]⊗M, |x|=1, at p=2, and Σ^{−1}R_+(M)=Λ(x)⊗F_p[y^{±1}]⊗M, |x|=1, |y|=2, at odd p. The action is twisted, not the ordinary diagonal action. On Σ^{−1}R_+(M), at p=2 set Sq^s(x^r⊗a)=Σ_{j≥0}binom(r−j,s−2j)x^{r+s−j}⊗Sq^j(a). At odd p set P^s(y^r⊗a)=Σ_j binom(r−(p−1)j,s−pj)y^{r+(p−1)(s−j)}⊗P^j(a)+Σ_j binom(r−(p−1)j−1,s−pj−1)xy^{r+(p−1)(s−j)−1}⊗βP^j(a); P^s(xy^{r−1}⊗a)=Σ_j binom(r−(p−1)j−1,s−pj)xy^{r+(p−1)(s−j)−1}⊗P^j(a); β(y^r⊗a)=0 and β(xy^{r−1}⊗a)=y^r⊗a. Here r∈Z, s≥0, binomial coefficients use integral upper indices and are reduced mod p, and terms with negative lower entry vanish. Transport this action through graded suspension to R_+(M). Define the degree-zero A_p-linear augmentation ε_M:R_+(M)→M by ε(Σx^{r−1}⊗a)=Sq^r(a) for r≥0 and zero for r<0 at p=2. At odd p first project onto the summand spanned by Σy^{(p−1)r}⊗a and Σxy^{(p−1)r−1}⊗a; for r≥0 send them to −(−1)^rβP^r(a) and (−1)^rP^r(a), respectively, and send r<0 to zero.
proofSteps: Define the underlying Laurent/exterior graded module and the displayed actions; use Cartan and Adem to show they extend to an A_p-action.
Check that the augmentation respects all generators of A_p, including the Bockstein and suspension signs.
Maps of M act coefficientwise; the formula and field tensor product show exactness and functoriality.

nodes.title: Singer Tor-equivalence
nodes.statement: For every graded A_p-module M, ε_M:R_+(M)→M induces an isomorphism Tor_{s,t}^{A_p}(F_p,R_+M)→Tor_{s,t}^{A_p}(F_p,M) for all s,t. More generally, a Tor-equivalence L→M induces Ext^{s,t}_{A_p}(M,N)≅Ext^{s,t}_{A_p}(L,N) whenever N is bounded below and degreewise finite-dimensional. In particular this holds for N=F_p. Neither M nor R_+M is assumed bounded below in the Tor statement.
proofSteps: For the finite Hopf subalgebras, localize the appropriate dual polynomial generator to form the bimodules used in AGM Lemma 2.1. The monomial basis makes each free over the left finite Hopf algebra and the preceding right one.
Pass to the filtered union: for free M the Singer module is A_p-flat and ε induces an isomorphism on F_p-coinvariants (AGM Lemma 2.2).
Apply the exact Singer functor to a free resolution of M and compare the two Tor spectral sequences; include the suspension converting AGM’s augmentation degree to LNR’s degree-zero ε.
For the Ext consequence dualize the cobar comparison into bounded-below finite-type N, where the degreewise products and inverse-limit arguments are controlled.
acceptance: Ext_A(M,F_p)→Ext_A(R_+M,F_p) is an isomorphism in every bidegree.
If N has the stated bounds, every A_p-linear map R_+M→N factors uniquely through ε_M.

nodes.title: The extended-power Singer approximation
nodes.statement: For B bounded below and degreewise finite type over F_p, form U_n(B)=Σ^{1+n}D_{C_p}(Σ^{−n}B), n≥0, with the bonding maps from inclusions of successive multiples of the reduced regular representation. There is a cofinal comparison U_n(B)≃(B^{⊗p})^{tC_p}[1−(p−1)n] to the Greenlees Tate tower. Here Z^{tC_p}[k] denotes its kth Greenlees filtration stage as in LNR Definition 4.3, not the suspension Σ^k(Z^{tC_p}); hence holim_n U_n(B)≃T_p(B). Each U_n(B) is individually bounded below and mod-p finite type, with no uniform lower bound asserted. The Tate tower and its generic norm construction remain imported from RT.2; this node owns the explicit cyclic extended-power approximation and its finiteness.
proofSteps: Model EC_p using the unit sphere in infinitely many reduced regular representations and use finite skeleta/representation inclusions to specify the tower maps.
Use equivariant duality for the finite representation spheres and the norm/isotropy-separation model to obtain the indicated shifted extended powers.
For a fixed truncation, only finitely many free cells occur in each dimension; boundedness below and degreewise finiteness of H*B give the same properties for that stage.
acceptance: The tower index tends to −∞ in the Tate truncation convention as n→∞.
No extra Σ or missing desuspension is allowed in the cofinal comparison.

nodes.statement: For B bounded below and degreewise finite type over F_p there is a natural graded A_p-isomorphism H_c^*(U_•(B);F_p)≅R_+(H*(B;F_p)). Under this isomorphism the map to H*(B;F_p) induced by Δ_p:B→T_pB equals ε_{H*B}. Equivalently colim_n H*(Σ^nD_{C_p}(Σ^{−n}B);F_p)≅Σ^{−1}R_+(H*B); the one-suspension difference from U_n is essential.
proofSteps: Calculate extended-power homology by the cyclic resolution and the tensor Künneth isomorphism. Split mixed tensor-basis words into free C_p-orbits, leaving the diagonal words; track the Steenrod action to obtain the Singer formulas.
Pass along the representation-sphere tower and keep its suspension shift, yielding the continuous-cohomology comparison.

Construct the geometric map B≃Φ^{C_p}(N_e^{C_p}B)→(B^{⊗p})^{tC_p}. It is natural, commutes with suspension and on S sends the unit to the canonical Tate unit; the exact-functor normalization in the imported Tate diagonal identifies it with Δ_p. No Segal equivalence is used for this identification.

Its map on continuous cohomology factors uniquely through ε by the bounded-target Hom consequence. Determine the residual endomorphism first on B=HF_p using the unit, then on suspensions, then on arbitrary cohomology classes represented by B→Σ^qHF_p.

nodes.title: Finite-type generalized Segal theorem
nodes.statement: For B bounded below and degreewise finite type over F_p, Δ_p:B→(B^{⊗p})^{tC_p} is a p-adic equivalence and its target is p-complete, so it exhibits the target as B_p^∧. In particular S→S^{tC_p} is the Segal conjecture for C_p (Lin at p=2, Gunawardena at odd p), and HF_p→(HF_p^{⊗p})^{tC_p} is an equivalence. The sphere case here is a computed consequence, not an input taken from the acceptance example of RT.2/tate-diagonal.
proofSteps: Compare the ordinary Adams spectral sequence for B with the inverse-limit Adams spectral sequence of U_•(B).
Use the continuous Singer comparison and ε Tor-equivalence to identify their E₂ pages. Apply strong convergence, including complete filtration comparison, to conclude a p-adic equivalence.
T_pB is p-complete by the imported bounded-below Tate theorem. Use the universal property of p-completion.

nodes.title: Finite towers with finite inverse limit
nodes.statement: Let S_0←S_1←⋯ be a tower of finite sets, and let L=lim_n S_n be finite; empty stages and an empty L are allowed. There is n_0 such that the projection L→S_n is injective for every n≥n_0. For every n there is m≥n with image(S_m→S_n)=image(L→S_n). Consequently the canonical morphism from the constant pro-set L to the tower S_• is a pro-isomorphism. For finite-group towers the same assertion holds as pro-groups. No surjectivity of the original transition maps is assumed.
proofSteps: Use finite ranges and the imported Mittag–Leffler criterion to replace the tower by its eventual-range system without changing sections.
If a stage or the limit is empty, compactness of finite compatible sections forces eventual emptiness at each fixed stage.
Otherwise eventual ranges form a surjective tower of nonempty finite sets. The baseline section-surjectivity and eventual-injectivity theorems give a separating stage for the finite section set.
At a fixed stage, its eventual range is the image of L by compactness, and finite decreasing images stabilize. Translate these two assertions to the explicit pro-isomorphism criterion.
acceptance: For a tower ℕᵒᵖ→Type, the Lean milestone states injectivity at one stage together with eventual image equality; later injectivity follows from transition compatibility.

A direct sum of copies of this same pro-group comparison stays pro-constant because a single later index works for all copies. This does not assert that arbitrary nonuniform families of pro-isomorphisms commute with direct sums.

The companion Lean theorem is named PowerOperations.finite_tower_pro_constant; its hypotheses are finiteness of every stage and of the compatible-family set, and its conclusion is a separating evaluation together with eventual image equality.

sources.match: A finite inverse limit of finite sets gives a constant pro-object; the stabilization is used uniformly over arbitrary direct sums.

nodes.title: Truncated tensor Tate functors
nodes.statement: For a prime p and n∈Z define T_p^{(n)}(X)=(τ_{≤n}(X^{⊗p}))^{tC_p}, using the coherent cyclic permutation action before truncation. There is a natural tower in n and a comparison T_p(X)→lim_{n→∞}T_p^{(n)}(X), which is an equivalence by RT.2’s Tate truncation theorem. For every fixed n, T_p^{(n)} preserves arbitrary direct sums of spectra: all mixed words have free C_p-orbits and are Tate-acyclic, while the surviving summands are uniformly bounded above before homotopy fixed points.
proofSteps: Truncate in the equivariant functor category and use the Tate truncation-limit comparison supplied by RT.2.
Expand a p-fold smash of a direct sum by words in the index set. Primality makes every nonconstant word a free cyclic orbit; truncation respects the induced decomposition.

Kill the induced summands by Tate vanishing. For the remaining uniformly coconnective summands, commute direct sums with homotopy fixed points using the finite cyclic resolution degree by degree. Homotopy orbits preserve all colimits.
For X=HF_p, use the Milnor finite-type coefficient theorem and the bounded Tate spectral sequence to prove each π_iT_p^{(n)}(HF_p) is finite.
acceptance: The arbitrary-sum assertion is only made at a fixed truncation n.

nodes.title: The arbitrary-dimensional HF_p case
nodes.statement: For every F_p-vector space V of arbitrary dimension, Δ_p:HV→(HV^{⊗p})^{tC_p} is an equivalence. In every homotopy degree i, the comparison from the constant pro-group π_iHV to the tower π_iT_p^{(n)}(HV) is a pro-isomorphism, with stabilization indices inherited from the single HF_p tower and independent of the dimension of V.
proofSteps: Choose a basis V≅⊕_JF_p and identify HV with the corresponding direct sum of HF_p spectra.
Each fixed truncation preserves this sum. The HF_p homotopy groups at each truncation are finite; Milnor’s sequence and finite-type Segal identify their inverse limit with the finite group π_iHF_p.
Apply the finite-tower pro-constant theorem. Tensor the same comparison with the free F_p-vector space on J, using a uniform index rather than commuting an arbitrary inverse limit with a sum.
The tower is pro-constant in each degree, so lim¹ vanishes. Milnor’s sequence identifies π_iT_p(HV) with π_iHV, compatibly with Δ_p.

nodes.title: The bounded-below generalized Segal conjecture
nodes.statement: For every bounded-below spectrum X and prime p, the Tate diagonal Δ_p:X→T_pX=(X^{⊗p})^{tC_p} exhibits T_pX as the derived p-completion X_p^∧, naturally in X and compatibly with the imported lax symmetric monoidal diagonal. There is no finite-generation assumption on the homotopy or homology groups. The bounded-below hypothesis is essential.
proofSteps: Shift X to be connective, using exactness of T_p. The tensor map X^{⊗p}→(τ_{≤n}X)^{⊗p} has connectivity tending to infinity. Homotopy orbits preserve these bounds and homotopy fixed points preserve limits, so T_pX≃lim_nT_p(τ_{≤n}X).
Completion commutes with limits by its function-spectrum model; exactness and finite Postnikov dévissage reduce to X=HM.
Resolve M by free abelian groups to reduce, by exactness, to p-torsion-free M. The target is p-complete by RT.2.
Mod-p detection and exactness reduce the assertion to H(M/pM), since multiplication by p is injective on M. Apply the arbitrary-vector theorem, then recover the completion statement.
acceptance: For X=S the result is the prime-order Segal conjecture; for X=HF_p it is an equivalence.
For X=H(⊕_JF_p) the statement is valid for every set J.
The proof never replaces T_p by a functor preserving unrestricted sums.

nodes.title: Weyl refinement of the Tate diagonal
nodes.statement: Fix C_p≤Σ_p generated by a p-cycle and W=N_{Σ_p}(C_p)/C_p≅F_p^×. The Tate diagonal has a unique lax symmetric monoidal refinement X→((X^{⊗p})^{tC_p})^{hW} whose forgetful map is Δ_p. For X=Σ∞_+Y it factors through (X^{⊗p})^{hΣ_p} by the suspension of the space diagonal. For an E∞-ring R, multiplication gives an E∞ refinement φ_R:R→(R^{tC_p})^{hW}. For R=S[M], M an E∞ space monoid, this factors through R^{hΣ_p}. The order p−1 is invertible on R^{tC_p}, so homotopy groups of its W-fixed points are algebraic W-invariants.
proofSteps: Apply the unit-normalized exact-functor construction to X↦((X^{⊗p})^{tC_p})^{hW}; uniqueness gives the forgetful compatibility.
For suspension spectra compare the two lax monoidal transformations using the initiality of Σ∞_+ and its space diagonal.
Multiply the tensor factors for R. The normalizer quotient has prime-to-p order, so averaging makes its group cohomology above zero vanish on the p-local Tate homotopy groups.
acceptance: The W-refinement does not assert a Tate construction for all of Σ_p.
Restriction from Σ_p homotopy fixed points uses the actual normalizer, with its coherent action.

nodes.title: Underlying-space diagonal factorization
nodes.statement: For every spectrum X, Ω∞ of the W-refined Tate diagonal equals the composite Ω∞X→((Ω∞X)^p)^{hΣ_p}→Ω∞(X^{⊗p})^{hΣ_p}→Ω∞((X^{⊗p})^{tC_p})^{hW}. The first map is the ordinary space diagonal, the second the lax monoidal comparison, and the last restriction followed by can. The equality is natural and lax symmetric monoidal; it is not an assertion of a natural spectrum map X→(X^{⊗p})^{hΣ_p}.
proofSteps: Form the space diagonal and apply the lax symmetric monoidal Ω∞ comparison.
Restrict along C_p⋊W≤Σ_p and apply can.
Use the unit normalization and initiality/universal property of Ω∞ to identify it with Ω∞Δ_p.
acceptance: The lift is at the level of spaces; it need not preserve the additive infinite-loop structure.

nodes.title: Positive-degree splitting of the norm sequence
nodes.statement: Let X be bounded below and p-complete, and put A=X^{⊗p} with cyclic permutation action. For every i≥1, the norm and the underlying-space diagonal give an isomorphism of abelian groups π_i(A^{hC_p})≅π_i(A_{hC_p})⊕π_i(X). In degree zero they give an exact sequence 0→π_0(A_{hC_p})→π_0(A^{hC_p})→π_0(X)→0 with a natural set section; no additive splitting is asserted in degree zero.
hypotheses: X bounded below and derived p-complete.
proofSteps: Identify A^{tC_p} with X by the p-complete generalized Segal theorem.
The space diagonal is a section of can after applying Ω∞, so the connecting maps vanish in nonnegative degrees.
On π_i for i≥1 any based space map induces a group homomorphism; use the exact norm sequence. On π_0 retain only the set-level section.

nodes.title: The transfer ideal for a prime power operation
nodes.statement: For the prime p and E∞-ring R, let I_p(R,X)⊂R⁰(X×BΣ_p) be the ideal generated by images of additive stable transfers from X×B(Σ_i×Σ_{p−i}) for 0<i<p. nodes.statement: For every commutative ring A, π₀(φ_{HA}):A→π₀((HA)^{tC_p})=A/pA sends a to a^p mod p, agreeing with Mathlib’s ordinary Frobenius after reduction to characteristic p. If R is an E∞-ring whose underlying spectrum is the p-completion of a finite spectrum, or a retract of a finite cell S_p^∧-module, can∘const:R→R^{tC_p} is an equivalence. Under this equivalence φ_R is an E∞ endomorphism. For the p-complete sphere this endomorphism is the identity.
proofSteps: For HA use the cyclic coefficient calculation and the degree-zero power on coefficients.

The constant-map comparison is an equivalence on S_p^∧ by the sphere Segal theorem and Tate p-completion invariance. Both sides are exact on finite cell S_p^∧-modules, so finite cofibers and retracts extend the comparison to the stated class. This is the finite/dualizable p-complete class needed for the spherical Witt example; no claim that S_p^∧ is categorically compact is used.

nodes.title: Spherical Witt vectors of a finite field
nodes.statement: Let k=F_{p^d}, d≥1. Define SW(k) to be the p-complete connective E∞-algebra étale over S_p^∧ whose π₀ is W(k), using the finite étale Z_p-algebra W(k). The imported spectral étale lifting equivalence makes this object unique up to contractible choice. Its underlying S_p^∧-module is finite free of rank d. Thus the Tate-valued Frobenius, after identifying the target with SW(k) by const/can, is the unique E∞ endomorphism inducing the Witt Frobenius on π₀. It reduces to a↦a^p on k.
proofSteps: Use the requested finite étale Witt-ring input W(F_{p^d}) over Z_p, then apply the existing spectral étale lifting theorem to S_p^∧. The ordinary Witt vectors are not redefined.
Spectral flatness gives π_iSW(k)=π_iS_p^∧⊗_{Z_p}W(k), so a Z_p-basis lifts to a finite-free module equivalence and places the underlying spectrum in the finite-cell S_p^∧-module class.

Compare φ with the zeroth Postnikov section and ordinary Frobenius. The finite étale Witt input says reduction determines the Z_p-algebra endomorphism; the spectral étale equivalence then gives uniqueness on the spectrum.
acceptance: Only finite fields are asserted here; no compactness claim for SW(k) for arbitrary perfect k is made.

nodes.title: Representation spheres and twisted cohomology
nodes.statement: For a space (anima) X and a real virtual vector bundle V on X, let S^V∈Fun(X,Sp) be its fiberwise invertible representation-sphere local system, with S^{−V} its tensor inverse. For p_X:X→pt define X^{−V}=p_{X,!}S^{−V} and R^V(X)=[X^{−V},R]. For an actual representation V of a finite group G, the corresponding S^V over BG is its one-point compactification with the full G-action; a virtual difference uses tensor inverse. For V the trivial rank-n virtual bundle, R^V(X)=R^n(X)=[Σ∞_+X,Σ^nR], for every n∈Z. This specializes the imported generic Thom-colimit construction and extends it to all virtual ranks; it does not require an orientation or a global finite-rank complementary bundle.
proofSteps: Use the stable J-construction: a linear bundle gives a family of one-point compactifications, and direct sums correspond to tensor products. Group-complete under direct sum to treat virtual bundles.

Apply the imported colimit/Thom formalism fiberwise; maps from the colimit give the adjunction description. For nontrivial virtual rank first split off the locally constant integer rank and use degree-zero R-lines on each component.
Identify the trivial-bundle case by commuting suspension with the colimit. For a representation over BG retain its coherent action; do not choose a nonequivariant trivialization.
acceptance: No orientability assumption is imposed on the bundle, since the twist retains orientation monodromy.

nodes.title: The representation Thom adjunction
nodes.statement: Let ρ be the p-dimensional permutation representation of Σ_p and n∈Z. There is a natural isomorphism R^{nρ}(X×BΣ_p)≅[Σ∞_+X,(S^{nρ}⊗R)^{hΣ_p}], where Σ_p acts trivially on R and nρ is pulled back from BΣ_p. This is valid for every space X and spectrum R, including n<0. It is induced by the p_!⊣p*⊣p_* adjunctions, not by choosing a Thom orientation.
proofSteps: Express the negative Thom object as the colimit of S^{−nρ} over X×BΣ_p.
Adjoint to a map of parametrised spectra and tensor with S^{nρ}.
Compose the right Kan extensions over X×BΣ_p→X→pt; their BΣ_p step is the homotopy-fixed-point spectrum.
acceptance: For n=0 the isomorphism reduces to R⁰(X×BΣ_p)≅[Σ∞_+X,R^{hΣ_p}].

nodes.title: Rezk power operations in every degree
nodes.statement: For an E∞-ring R, a prime p and n∈Z define P_p^n:Ω∞Σ^nR→Ω∞(S^{nρ}⊗R)^{hΣ_p} by the space diagonal, the lax monoidal Ω∞ comparison, the equivariant equivalence (Σ^nR)^{⊗p}≃S^{nρ}⊗R^{⊗p}, and multiplication. Via the Thom adjunction this gives P_p^n:R^n(X)→R^{nρ}(X×BΣ_p). It is a natural operation of sets of cohomology classes; neither additivity nor an ordinary untwisted target is built into its definition.
proofSteps: Apply the space diagonal to Ω∞Σ^nR and then the lax monoidal comparison.
Retain the permutation representation on the suspension factors, including inverse representation spheres when n<0.
Postcompose multiplication and use the Thom adjunction to obtain an operation on every space X.
acceptance: For n=0 this is exactly the earlier degree-zero power operation.

nodes.title: Representation-suspension Tate comparison
nodes.statement: For any E∞-ring spectrum R and n∈Z there is a natural equivalence Σ^n((R^{tC_p})^{hW})≃((S^{nρ}⊗R)^{tC_p})^{hW}, where the right-hand action is inherited from the normalizer of C_p in Σ_p. This identifies the target of Σ^nφ_R with the Tate target of P_p^n. The representation has dimension np but the Tate suspension comparison shifts by n, and it holds for negative n as well.
proofSteps: In Mod_R consider M↦((M^{⊗_Rp})^{tC_p})^{hW}, with tensor action before Tate.
The mixed terms are induced and vanish, exactly as for T_p; hence this relative functor is exact.
Compare its value on Σ^nR with Σ^n of its value on R. The tensor suspension is S^{nρ}, giving the displayed equivalence.
acceptance: At n=0 the comparison is the identity.
No ordinary Σ^{np} suspension equivalence with trivial group action is substituted.

sources.match: Exactness of the relative p-fold tensor Tate functor on R-modules produces the all-integer suspension equivalence.

nodes.title: Extended-power and Thom descriptions of power
nodes.statement: The operation P_p^n agrees with the following classical Thom construction. For a virtual bundle V over X, the extended power of a representative X^{−V}→R and the E∞ multiplication define a class in R^{D_pV}(D_pX), with D_pX=(X^p)_{hΣ_p} and D_pV its fiberwise sum bundle. The Thom comparison is D_p(X^{−V})≃(D_pX)^{−D_pV}. When V is the trivial rank-n bundle, pullback along the diagonal X×BΣ_p→D_pX has twist nρ and gives P_p^n. This applies to all virtual n.
proofSteps: Use tensor compatibility and iterated colimits of parametrised spheres to prove the displayed Thom comparison; it includes virtual negative bundles by invertibility.
Apply D_p to the representing map and then its E∞ multiplication to get the class over D_pX.
Pull back along the Borel diagonal. Adjoint to the representing map using the Thom adjunction; the resulting map is the definition of P_p^n.
acceptance: The all-degree comparison uses homotopy orbits in D_pX and homotopy fixed points in the representing target; these are related by adjunction, not identified with one another.

sources.match: The map-level operation on Ω∞Σ^nR coincides with the extended-power Thom model.

nodes.title: Frobenius and power operations in all degrees
nodes.statement: For every E∞-ring R, space X, n∈Z and prime p, postcomposition with Σ^nφ_R equals R^n(X)→R^{nρ}(X×BΣ_p)→[Σ∞_+X,((S^{nρ}⊗R)^{tC_p})^{hW}]≅[Σ∞_+X,Σ^n((R^{tC_p})^{hW})]. The first map is P_p^n, the second is restriction to the normalizer followed by can, and the last is the inverse of the Tate-suspension equivalence. This is the precise comparison of the spectral Frobenius with classical power operations, including negative degrees.
proofSteps: Exactness identifies Σ^nΔ_R with Δ_{Σ^nR} under the corresponding Tate-suspension comparison.
The compatibility of multiplication with that comparison gives the target comparison of the Frobenius.
Apply the underlying-space diagonal theorem to Σ^nR, then the Thom and extended-power comparison, and take maps from X.
acceptance: The n=0 specialization is exactly the earlier degree-zero comparison.
The theorem imposes no boundedness hypothesis on R; boundedness was needed for the Segal equivalence, not for constructing or comparing these maps.

nodes.title: Eilenberg–MacLane Tate decompositions
nodes.statement: As HF_p-modules, (HF_2)^{tC_2}≃∏_{j∈Z}Σ^jHF_2. At odd p, ((HF_p)^{tC_p})^{hW}≃∏_{j∈Z}(Σ^{2j(p−1)}HF_p⊕Σ^{2j(p−1)+1}HF_p). Likewise (HZ)^{tC_2}≃∏_{j∈Z}Σ^{2j}HF_2, and at odd p ((HZ)^{tC_p})^{hW}≃∏_{j∈Z}Σ^{2j(p−1)}HF_p. Choose these splittings by the coefficient generators of PO.1. Because only finitely many summands contribute to each homotopy degree, the corresponding sum-to-product maps are equivalences; mapping an arbitrary spectrum into this product still gives a product of operation components.
proofSteps: Calculate coefficients by the cyclic resolution and W weights.
An HF_p-module splits degreewise because F_p is a field. For HZ Tate, use the periodic resolution to exhibit the two-term pieces with differential p, each quasi-isomorphic to a shifted F_p.
Take W-invariants by averaging and select only weights divisible by p−1. Use degreewise finiteness of summands to compare their sum and product.
acceptance: The summand carrying P¹ at odd p is Σ^{2(p−1)}HF_p.
The map φ_{HF_p} is generally not HF_p-linear; only its target decomposition is an HF_p-module splitting.

sources.match: The module decompositions separate the components of the total Frobenius; the odd-primary shifts have the corrected factor two.

nodes.title: Steenrod components of the ordinary power
nodes.statement: With the coefficient normalization s,t,e in PO.1, applying can to P_p^n and then the Tate-suspension comparison has coefficients Sq^i at p=2, and P^i and βP^i at odd p. Equivalently, on a homogeneous x∈H^n(X;F_p) of a space, the resulting degree-n class is Σ_{i≥0}Sq^i(x)s^i at p=2, and Σ_{i≥0}P^i(x)t^{(p−1)i}+Σ_{i≥0}βP^i(x)t^{(p−1)i}e at odd p. Each term has total degree n. The expression denotes the coefficientwise product decomposition; for an ordinary space and a fixed homogeneous class instability makes these displayed sums finite. It is not an unqualified tensor-product description of cohomology for arbitrary unbounded spectra.
proofSteps: Use the extended-power Thom comparison to identify P_p^n with the ordinary-cohomology power operation used to construct the Steenrod operations.
Use the Thom class/Euler normalization to track the suspension and the coefficients s^i or t^{(p−1)i}, including the Bockstein coefficient e.
At odd p check W weights and the factor 2 in the degree. Apply instability only to classes on spaces.
acceptance: For u∈H¹(RP∞;F_2), the formula gives u+u²s.
For v∈H²(CP∞;F_p), odd p, the formula gives v+v^p t^{p−1}, with zero Bockstein terms.

nodes.title: Frobenius as the total Steenrod operation
nodes.statement: Under the chosen product decomposition, φ_{HF_2}:HF_2→(HF_2)^{tC_2} has component Sq^i:HF_2→Σ^iHF_2 for i≥0 and zero components for i<0. At odd p, φ_{HF_p}:HF_p→((HF_p)^{tC_p})^{hW} has components P^i:HF_p→Σ^{2i(p−1)}HF_p and βP^i:HF_p→Σ^{2i(p−1)+1}HF_p for i≥0, with negative-index components zero. For HZ the components are Sq^{2i}∘r at p=2, and P^i∘r at odd p, i≥0, where r:HZ→HF_p is reduction. Evaluation on spaces is the total-operation formula of the previous theorem. This is an equality of spectrum maps, not just of maps on π₀.
proofSteps: The all-degree Frobenius theorem identifies evaluation with the power coefficients just computed.

For each Eilenberg–MacLane target summand, identify the corresponding stable operation using representability and the complete stable Steenrod-operation algebra, retaining the all-degree comparisons. Product universality gives equality of the spectrum maps; do not assume φ is HF_p-linear.
Use naturality under HZ→HF_p and the coefficient map on Tate to obtain the integral variant, eliminating the odd-square/Bockstein summands.
acceptance: The i=0 component is the identity for HF_p and reduction for HZ.
For p=3, P¹ has target Σ⁴HF_3 and βP¹ has target Σ⁵HF_3.
The higher components may be nonzero although all positive homotopy groups of HF_p itself vanish.

nodes.title: Atiyah cyclic power in K-theory
nodes.statement: For a finite CW pair (X,A), construct Atiyah’s cyclic power on KU⁰(X,A) by the C_p-equivariant p-fold tensor product of complexes of vector bundles, followed by restriction along the diagonal and the Borel construction. For an actual bundle V its fiber is V^{⊗p}, with C_p rotating the factors. Extend to virtual classes using the complex/difference construction, not by declaring tensor power additive. For absolute X this gives KU⁰(X)→KU⁰(X×BC_p)^{W}. This is the restriction of the E∞ KU power operation P_p⁰.
proofSteps: Use equivariant tensor products of relative complexes, with Koszul signs for complex degrees, and pass through the difference construction.
Prove homotopy and acyclic-complex invariance and compare the resulting operation with the E∞ KU multiplication using the splitting principle and the additive transfer formula.
Restriction from Σ_p makes the result invariant under the cyclic normalizer.
acceptance: For a line bundle L, the cyclic generator acts trivially on the line L^{⊗p}; evaluation at a p-cycle gives L^p.

nodes.title: Tate coefficients of periodic K-theory
nodes.statement: For KU with trivial C_{p^r}-action, r=1,2, choose the multiplicative coordinate x=L−1. Then π_*KU^{tC_{p^r}} is KU_*((x))/((1+x)^{p^r}−1), interpreted by the Euler-inversion/completed-cohomology construction, and is KU_*⊗_Z(⊕_{j=1}^r Q_p(ζ_{p^j})); the finite direct sum is also the product ring. The spectra are rational, even periodic, and have no odd homotopy. For r=1, W acts by the cyclotomic Galois action on Q_p(ζ_p) and fixes KU_*, so the constant-map comparison gives KU_p^∧[1/p]≃(KU^{tC_p})^{hW}.
proofSteps: Use the complex orientation and the skeletal filtration of BC_{p^r} to compute KU⁰(BC_{p^r}) by the multiplicative p^r-series, with the completion dictated by the filtration.

The representation-sphere model of Tate inverts the Euler class x. In the resulting quotient inverting x forces p to be invertible. Factor the p^r-series into cyclotomic factors and use their coprimality after inversion to obtain the indicated fields.

Compute the normalizer action on a chosen root of unity; invariants of Q_p(ζ_p) are Q_p. The constant map sends the coefficient and Bott classes to their usual images, giving the spectrum equivalence.
acceptance: At p=2, KU^{tC_2} has even homotopy Q_2 and KU^{tC_4} has even homotopy Q_2⊕Q_2(i).
The p-series has zero constant term; the coordinate uses (1+x)^p−1, not the misprinted series of Example I.2.3.
This comparison equivalence is induced by the constant map, not by the Frobenius whose Bott action is different.

nodes.title: The KU Frobenius is the stable Adams operation
nodes.statement: Under (KU^{tC_p})^{hW}≃KU_p^∧[1/p], the refined Tate-valued Frobenius is the composite KU→KU[1/p]→KU_p^∧[1/p], whose first arrow is the imported stable Adams operation ψ^p. For a compact object X of spaces (a homotopy retract of a finite CW complex), on KU⁰(X) this is ψ^p followed by KU⁰(X)→KU⁰(X)⊗Q_p. It sends the homotopy Bott class β∈π₂KU to pβ. The unstable Adams operation on KU⁰ does not extend to a stable self-map KU→KU with that Bott action: the target must invert p.
proofSteps: Apply the degree-zero Frobenius comparison to KU and use the Atiyah compatibility. Cyclic character evaluation kills the transfer/regular-representation part and leaves ψ^p.
Use splitting into line bundles to identify the operation on KU⁰ of finite CW complexes and their retracts.

Test the reduced class on S² to obtain β↦pβ. The imported Snaith–Adams construction identifies the E∞ map after inverting p, then the constant-map coefficient equivalence supplies p-completion and rationalization.

For p=2, β goes to 2β; sending β to β would identify the constant map rather than Frobenius.
Topological compact Hausdorffness alone is not the meaning of compact space in this statement.

nodes.title: A counterexample to unbounded Tate fixpoint vanishing
nodes.statement: Give S the trivial C_{p²}-action. Then (S^{hC_p})^{t(C_{p²}/C_p)}≃S_p^∧≠0. Thus the conclusion of the bounded-above Tate fixpoint lemma cannot be applied to the sphere. The residual quotient action is the coherent action induced by the C_{p²}-extension, not an independently assigned trivial action on S^{hC_p}.
proofSteps: Apply the residual Tate construction to S_{hC_p}→S^{hC_p}→S^{tC_p}.
The first term vanishes by the bounded-below Tate orbit lemma. The sphere Segal equivalence identifies the last original term with S_p^∧ equivariantly for the trivial quotient action.
Apply Tate p-completion invariance and the sphere Segal equivalence once more to obtain the result.
acceptance: π₀ of the iterated Tate spectrum is Z_p, so it is not contractible.

sources.match: The sphere’s homotopy fixed points give a nonzero iterated Tate spectrum.

nodes.title: A counterexample to unbounded Tate orbit vanishing
nodes.statement: For KU with trivial C_{p²}-action the Tate orbit conclusion (KU_{hC_p})^{t(C_{p²}/C_p)}≃0 fails. Indeed the natural comparison KU^{tC_{p²}}→(KU^{tC_p})^{h(C_{p²}/C_p)} is not an equivalence: in each even degree its source has coefficient Q_p(ζ_p)⊕Q_p(ζ_{p²}), whereas its target has Q_p(ζ_p). Odd homotopy groups are zero.
proofSteps: The coherent residual action on KU^{tC_p} extends to the connected circle quotient, so it acts trivially on homotopy groups.
For this rational spectrum higher finite-group cohomology vanishes, so the residual homotopy fixed points have unchanged coefficients.
Compare the two Tate coefficient calculations. The orbit-vanishing condition would imply an equivalence by the norm comparison argument; the dimensions differ.
acceptance: At p=2 the two even coefficient spaces have Q_2-dimensions 3 and 1.

nodes.title: Failure of Segal completion for unbounded spectra
nodes.statement: At p=2, T_2(KU)=(KU⊗KU)^{tC_2}, with C_2 swapping factors, is rational. Therefore Δ_2:KU→T_2(KU) does not exhibit the target as KU_2^∧: the latter has nonzero mod-2 cofiber, whereas a rational spectrum has zero mod-2 cofiber. nodes.statement: For every based simply connected space Y, the standard cosimplicial free-loop model Y^{n+1} has a comparison Σ∞_+LY→Tot_{[n]∈Δ}Σ∞_+(Y^{n+1}) which is an equivalence. The same statement holds after any fixed p-fold edgewise subdivision, with terms Y^{p(n+1)} and its coherent C_p-action. The fibers of successive partial-totalization stages have connectivity tending to +∞. No finite CW or finite-type hypothesis on Y is imposed. This is a theorem for this cosimplicial model, not preservation of arbitrary limits by Σ∞_+.

Analyze the normalized fiber at cosimplicial degree n≥1: it is built from Ω^nΣ∞Y^{∧n} and Ω^nΣ∞Y^{∧(n+1)}. Since Y is 1-connected their connectivity grows with n; retain the reduced suspension spectrum in these terms.

For arbitrary simply connected Y, express it as a filtered homotopy colimit of finite simply connected models. At each fixed totalization stage the construction is finite; increasing connectivity lets the filtered colimit commute with the complete totalization degree by degree, as in Malkiewich’s proof.

nodes.title: Tate commutation with a controlled totalization
nodes.statement: Let Z_• be a tower of spectra with coherent finite G-action, and suppose the connectivity of fib(holim_mZ_m→Z_n) tends to +∞. Apply this to the partial totalizations of the edgewise-subdivided free-loop model from the preceding theorem. The connectivity hypothesis is essential to the orbit step.
proofSteps: Homotopy orbits preserve the given connectivity bounds by their bar realization/connective t-structure compatibility.

For a fixed degree, the maps from the limit to a sufficiently late stage induce stable isomorphisms, before and after homotopy orbits. Milnor’s sequence therefore identifies the orbit comparison as an equivalence.
Homotopy fixed points are limits and commute with all limits. Take the cofiber of the natural norm comparison; finite limits and colimits agree in Sp.
Finite partial totalizations commute with Tate by exactness, so the tower result yields the cosimplicial comparison.

Commute Tate through this totalization using the connectivity theorem, and commute p-completion with limits using its function-spectrum model. This proves the first assertion.
